close_reason: Pinned last-write-wins semantics with two tests (intra-batch + pre-populated collision), both verified to fail under first-write-wins flip. Expanded dispatch call-site comment to document both collision flavours and the rationale (RFC ambiguous, wire-behaviour change out of scope for a foundation crate without RFC mandate). The 'at minimum a log line' option from the bead's recommendation hierarchy was blocked by the crate's sealed dep set (AGENTS.md: no tracing). The 'at most: reject' option was rejected as wire-behaviour change in canonical foundation crate. Landed at the bead's documented floor: explicit encoding + test so a refactor flipping the order does not silently change behaviour.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:236-291 — the dispatcher merges client-pre-populated createdIds with server-assigned ones via HashMap::insert in extract_created_ids_into. If a /set response reports created.client-X.id = "server-new" and the client pre-populated createdIds with the same key client-X mapped to "server-old" (e.g. a long-lived background task replaying a queued request), the pre-populated value is silently overwritten.

Test created_ids_merges_with_pre_populated_map (lib.rs:864) covers the disjoint-key case (client-old and client-new are different keys). It does NOT cover the collision case where a /set call returns a creationId that was already in the pre-populated map.

RFC 8620 §3.4 is ambiguous on which semantics is correct, but the silent overwrite is the more surprising one: a client that pre-populates createdIds is reasonably treating that map as authoritative, and a server-generated mapping for the same client-id is a sign of a logic error somewhere — not a value to silently prefer.

Trigger: any client that pre-populates createdIds AND a backend that mis-reports a creationId that collides. The current dispatcher returns the server-assigned value; the client-supplied one disappears with no error.

Recommendation: at least add a debug_assert that detects pre-populated-key collision in extract_created_ids_into and surfaces it as a serverFail (or at minimum a log line). At most: reject the collision as a serverFail invocation for the offending /set call. The existing comment at lib.rs:276-289 mentions intra-batch duplicates only; the pre-populated-then-collided case is undocumented and untested.

If "last write wins" is the deliberate semantics, a test should encode it explicitly so a future refactor that changes the order does not silently flip the behaviour.
title: Pre-populated createdIds silently overwritten by /set responses
